issues.title: Full document re-sorting by debiased scores disrupts distractor ordering
issues.description: The original debiased method sorted ALL documents by debiased scores, which changed the ordering of distractor documents. Per-example analysis showed 9 of 13 accuracy losses vs k=1 had identical gold-doc positions -- the losses were purely from distractor reordering affecting generation quality. Fix: minimal-swap strategy that sorts by raw attention (same as k=1) and only swaps the debiased top-1 document to the last position when it differs from the raw top-1. This preserves >99% of k=1's distractor ordering.

issues.title: Debiased ranking correctly identifies gold doc but full sort wastes the advantage
issues.description: Debiased ranking achieved 444/600 gold-at-last vs 425/600 for raw k=1 (19 extra corrections, 0 regressions). But the full re-sort introduced new generation failures that offset this ranking gain. The minimal-swap approach captures the ranking correction (10 swaps across 600 examples, all correctly identifying gold doc) without the distractor disruption cost.

summary: Replaced full-sort debiased approach with minimal-swap strategy: sort by raw attention scores (same as k=1), then swap only the debiased top-1 document to last position when it differs from raw top-1. This improved accuracy from 94.33% to 94.83% (+0.50pp) by eliminating the distractor reordering noise that caused 9 regression cases. The optimized method matches k=1 uncalibrated exactly (94.83%) and produces identical answers on all 600 examples. The gap to k=5 (95.50%) remains because the model is already robust to small position changes -- swapping the gold doc to last position doesn't change the model's answer when it's already in the top few positions after k=1 sorting.
